prompt.context: Your client is the CFO of Aperture Laboratories, a leading US biopharmaceutical company with a market cap greater than $150B. Aperture develops and manufactures a diversified range of products and in particular prides itself on saving millions of human lives every year. The company is under investor pressure because of its slow firm value growth over the next 10 years. Investors are very anxious to see significant changes announced at the firm in the next quarter. The CFO has already identified and evaluated a number of high-growth, promising, but capital-intensive projects, and she does not have enough cash to invest in any of the opportunities.
prompt.question: What does the CFO need to do next?

clarifying_info.a: Yes, the company is profitable but does not have sufficient free cash to fund the capital-intensive growth projects.

clarifying_info.q: Are there tax implications from any asset sale?
clarifying_info.a: Any divestiture deal has been structured by JP Morgan to be tax-free.

clarifying_info.q: Does the NPV of the projects include the capital investment?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the NPV figures shown include the capital investment required.

exhibits.title: Aperture Business Segments
exhibits.shows: A bubble/scatter chart plotting Aperture's eight business segments by Sales ($B) on the x-axis and 5-year CAGR on the y-axis. Segments are also positioned along an 'Increasing specialization requirements' dimension. Each segment is shown as a labeled data point.

exhibits.title: Investment Opportunities
exhibits.shows: A scatter chart plotting six potential projects by Capital Investment Required ($B) on the x-axis and Project NPV ($B) on the y-axis. Each project is labeled with its name.

projects.name: Cost-cutting initiative in US manufacturing plants
Research new formulations for existing product portfolio

framework: Raise capital: identify and evaluate options — issue equity, raise debt, divest a business unit, cancel or delay existing capital projects to free up budget
Evaluate divestiture candidates using the business segment data (growth, fit, specialization, ease of finding buyers)
Quantify proceeds from the chosen divestiture
Allocate capital across growth projects to maximize NPV within the capital constraint
Assess qualitative factors and risks for each project and the divestiture
Provide a recommendation with risk mitigations and next steps

questions.prompt: Walk through Exhibit 1 and recommend which business unit Aperture should divest, with rationale.
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify Animal Health as the best divestiture candidate. Key reasons: (1) among the lowest 5-yr CAGR (~3.1%) in the portfolio; (2) least aligned with Aperture's core mission of saving human lives; (3) low specialization requirements means a larger pool of potential buyers and easier transition. Candidate should also acknowledge the large sales base ($4.2B) makes it a meaningful source of capital.

questions.prompt: JP Morgan has assessed that Aperture will receive a 3.5x EV/Sales multiple for the Animal Health business. How much capital will the divestiture raise?
questions.guidance: Candidate should multiply Animal Health sales by the EV/Sales multiple to arrive at total proceeds. Should note the deal is structured to be tax-free. Should then transition to discussing which projects to fund.

math.setup: Enterprise Value = Animal Health Sales ($B) x EV/Sales multiple
math.answer: $14.7B in capital raised from the divestiture

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, which projects should Aperture invest in given the $14.7B capital constraint? Maximize total NPV.
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply a profitability index (NPV / Capital Investment) to rank projects, then select projects in descending order until the budget is exhausted. Strong candidates also discuss qualitative factors (project timeline, strategic fit, execution risk). The optimal selection is: (1) Build R&D center in China (PI=1.67), (2) License respiratory products from competitor (PI=1.67), (3) Cost-cutting initiative in US manufacturing plants (PI=1.40) — total capex $14B, total NPV $22B. The remaining $700M should be addressed (e.g., share buyback, dividend).

math.setup: Profitability Index = Project NPV / Capital Investment Required; rank descending and select until cumulative capex <= $14.7B
steps: Rank by PI: China R&D (1.67) = License respiratory (1.67) > US cost-cutting (1.40) > Sales force rationalization (1.25) > GLP-1 agonist (1.11) > New formulations (1.00)
Select China R&D ($6B) + License respiratory ($3B) + US cost-cutting ($5B) = $14B capex, $22B NPV
Remaining capital: $14.7B - $14.0B = $0.7B (recommend share buyback or dividend)
math.answer: Invest in Build R&D center in China, License respiratory products, and Cost-cutting initiative in US manufacturing plants for total NPV of $22B at $14B capex; return remaining $700M to shareholders

recommendation: Divest the Animal Health business unit at a 3.5x EV/Sales multiple to raise $14.7B in tax-free capital

Invest $14B of the proceeds across three projects: Build R&D center in China ($6B capex, $10B NPV), License respiratory products from a competitor ($3B capex, $5B NPV), and Cost-cutting initiative in US manufacturing plants ($5B capex, $7B NPV), generating a combined NPV of $22B
Return the remaining ~$700M to shareholders via share buyback or special dividend to signal financial discipline to investors
risks: Inability to find a willing buyer for the Animal Health division at the target multiple
Timing risk: deal completion and capital deployment may take longer than one quarter, frustrating investors
Execution risk on the new capital projects (R&D failure, licensing negotiations break down, cost-cutting delivers less than projected NPV)
Integration and transition complexity when divesting a $4.2B revenue business unit
next_steps: Engage JP Morgan to formally launch the Animal Health sale process and identify strategic and financial buyers
Obtain management and board buy-in for the divestiture and the three selected investment projects
Establish a project governance structure with milestones and KPIs for each of the three investments
Prepare investor communications announcing the strategic pivot ahead of the next quarterly earnings call
